title: audit current ADDR_CANON_FR
headline: ADDR_CANON_FR is 68 entries / 30 canonical values. It is already fully self-mapped, so the long-standing 'missing self-map loop entry' defect does NOT apply to it. The real new defect is that the 7-key exclusion tuple at normalize.py:321 is a provable no-op, and the dictionary maps only 17.54% of retained French address-token mass. Separately, build_profile.py and normalize.py use different tokenisers, so profile token counts over-count French elision particles and accent fragments.

dictionary_facts.method: ast.literal_eval of the module-level assignment; no import of polars, no dataset read

effective_france_canon_size.note: the naive overlap |FR INTERSECT COMMON| = 23 OVER-counts by exactly 4; the extra 4 are dr, n, st, ste, which the exclusion tuple removes from COMMON and ADDR_CANON_FR then re-adds. The merge is a {**base, **FR} overwrite, not an add.

defect_1_exclusion_tuple_is_a_noop.claim: All 7 excluded keys are IDENTITY self-maps in ADDR_CANON_COMMON, and 4 of the 7 (st, ste, dr, n) are immediately re-added by ADDR_CANON_FR. Only s, e, w are actually dropped, and dropping an identity self-map is indistinguishable from leaving it in, because canon.get(t, t) returns t in both cases.
defect_1_exclusion_tuple_is_a_noop.nature_of_that_diff: identity self-map -> unmapped; both emit the same string

measured_france_direction_token_counts.source: addr_tokens['France'] summed over test_s1, test_s2, test_s3

defect_1_exclusion_tuple_is_a_noop.conclusion: The tuple never suppresses English direction words in French addresses. That apparent effect comes entirely from ADDR_CANON_FR redefining st/ste/n, never from the removal. ne (6,465) and se (556) survive as evidence.

self_map_question_resolved.reason: all 29 non-empty canonical values already exist as keys mapping to themselves; adding ADDR_CANON_FR to the loop would setdefault(v, v) for values already present with identical values, i.e. zero behavioural change.

contrast_FR_REGIONS.verdict: FR_REGIONS genuinely DOES need the loop; ADDR_CANON_FR does not. The existing narrative conflates the two dictionaries.

defect_2_non_fixed_point_canonical_value.why_not_contaminating: token_idf is keyed on (country, tok) - features.py:19-20
defect_2_non_fixed_point_canonical_value.measured_effect_on_this_dataset: ZERO - none of street, str, strt, suite, north occurs in any French address

coverage.mass_basis: union of addr_tokens['France'] (top-4000) over test_s1, test_s2, test_s3
coverage.interpretation: ADDR_CANON_FR is a narrow street-type canonicaliser, not a general French address dictionary. INFERENCE, marked as such.
coverage.never_fire_caveat: NOT proven absent from the data. build_profile.py:27 keeps only TOPN=4000 and prune() at build_profile.py:45-49 drops count<=1 every 8 chunks, so a key occurring once in 480 MB is invisible. Rarest visible key is 'gal' at 25. Absence != zero.

function_words_by_source.note: rebuilt independently; test_s2 reproduces the already-established 15.41% exactly. New information: the rate is source-dependent, so the France-wide statement is a range, not a single number.
function_words_by_source.france_wide_statement: 15.41% to 19.52% depending on source; do not quote a single number

country_scoping.other_consumer_in_upstream: none; prep.py:13 is the only call site of normalize_address
country_scoping.scoping_direction: ONE-DIRECTIONAL - the overlay adds FR entries on top of ADDR_CANON_COMMON but never removes COMMON's India-specific aliases (bengaluru, gurgaon, nagar, taluk, colony, ...)

measured_french_exposure_to_india_aliase.verdict: benign at present, but the protection is accidental rather than designed

token_deletion_mass.mechanism: empty canon value => token dropped at normalize.py:348-349 (if t: ctoks.append(t))
token_deletion_mass.interpretation: INFERENCE, not measured: n/no are the French numero marker, so deleting them is correct behaviour. Not verified against raw strings - the profile does not retain them.

defect_3_tokeniser_divergence.status: NEW - affects the evidence base, not the pipeline
defect_3_tokeniser_divergence.profile_tokeniser: build_profile.py:28 TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r'[a-z0-9]+') applied to the RAW lowercased address
defect_3_tokeniser_divergence.pipeline_tokeniser: normalize.py:264-266 strip_accents, then normalize.py:269 _non_alnum = re.compile(r'[^a-z0-9]+'), plus normalize.py:342 c.replace(chr(39), '')

impossible_tokens_direct_evidence.note: a pipeline tokenisation can never emit these; they are pure profile artefacts

coeur.origin: coeur ligature, not decomposed by NFKD

apostrophe_glyph_inconsistency.normalize_py_342: strips only ASCII U+0027; typographic U+2019 is NOT stripped and NFKD does not decompose it
apostrophe_glyph_inconsistency.frequency: GAP - the profile's [a-z0-9]+ treats both glyphs identically, so the split cannot be measured. Inconsistency proven from source; impact unquantified.

aggregate_evidence.note: l and d are overwhelmingly apostrophe fragments of l'/d'; the pipeline joins those (leglise, dazur) and never emits standalone l or d. 36 distinct 1-char tokens is implausible for real address vocabulary.

defect_3_tokeniser_divergence.consequence: Profile token counts remain valid as evidence that a WORD occurs, but are NOT valid as evidence of how many tokens the pipeline will see. Any dictionary mined from profile counts is mined from a different tokeniser than the one that runs. Treat French profile token counts as upper bounds.

recommendations.rationale: zero effect; all 29 non-empty values already self-map

recommendations.action: Remove the 7-key exclusion tuple at normalize.py:321, or replace it with a comment stating it is inert.
recommendations.rationale: it is a provable no-op; there is nothing to fix

recommendations.action: Align build_profile.py:28 with normalize.py:264-266,342 - apply strip_accents and apostrophe removal before findall.
recommendations.rationale: highest value per line of code; unblocks accurate mining for every follow-on task

recommendations.action: If direction-word suppression is genuinely wanted for France, add north, south, east, west, ne, se, nw, sw explicitly.
recommendations.rationale: the current tuple does not do it; zero of these long forms occur in French data today, so this is hygiene not a score fix

recommendations.action: No change to the 68 entries themselves on the basis of this task.
recommendations.rationale: the coverage gap is real but dominated by geography words handled by FR_REGIONS, a separate open question

recommendations.action: Extend the profile with per-component token attribution.
recommendations.rationale: would let a later task measure false canonicalisation of city names
